scope: Woodford, Interest and Prices, Chapter 4: A Neo-Wicksellian Framework for the Analysis of Monetary Policy, with Appendix C. The basic model as exact derivatives and the natural rate of interest (Prop 4.1); Schur-Cohn root-location criteria for quadratics and cubics (Props C.1, C.2) and a proved Blanchard-Kahn theory for 2x2 forward systems and 3x3 systems with one predetermined variable (with the genericity condition the book omits); determinacy under exogenous, Taylor, inertial, forward-looking and price-level rules (Props 4.2-4.7; Prop 4.4 corrected; Prop 4.6 necessity); E-stability under sample-mean and regression learning with a Kronecker spectrum theorem (Props 4.8, 4.9) and Preston's long-horizon forms; determinants of inflation, targeting rules and the zero lower bound; money with non-separable utility; fiscal requirements and Prop 4.11 (with its non-degeneracy condition).
source: Michael Woodford, Interest and Prices: Foundations of a Theory of Monetary Policy, Princeton University Press, 2003, Chapter 4, pp. 237-319, and Appendix C, pp. 670-686.
